parts.title: Part 1 · Short texts
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Why is Anne texting?
questions.explanation: Anne updates Eric on her arrival and explains that the tickets are already booked. She also asks where to meet him at the theatre, so the message concerns their existing arrangement.
questions.evidence: The traffic’s awful but I’m almost there.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct statement about the careers talk.
questions.explanation: The talk has room for no more than thirty students, so students need to register quickly. It is for final-year students and concerns doing well after starting a job.
questions.evidence: Space for a maximum of thirty students, so sign up now.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct meaning of the recycling centre notice.
questions.explanation: Glass, plastic and metal items must be cleaned before people bring them in. Staff help users find the right bin rather than doing the cleaning for them.
questions.evidence: Glass, plastic and metal items must be cleaned before you bring them to the recycling centre.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct meaning of Gabriel’s message.
questions.explanation: Gabriel asks Nora who else he should buy tickets for. He is asking her to suggest other people who might like to attend the disco.
questions.evidence: Besides you, who else should I get tickets for?

questions.prompt: Choose the correct meaning of the restaurant notice.
questions.explanation: Customers can ask their waiter for information about ingredients while choosing a dish. The notice does not say that the menu itself lists all the ingredients.
questions.evidence: If you need information about the ingredients in any of our dishes, please tell your waiter

parts.title: Part 2 · Matching
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer. Match each person to the most suitable option. There are three extra options.

questions.prompt: Erika wants to see a show with music and which has famous actors in the lead roles. She’d like it to be based on a book and contain many different types of music.
questions.explanation: The End of Summer comes from a novel, features stars known from television and uses songs in many styles. It therefore meets all three of Erika’s requirements.
questions.evidence: the wide variety of music the producers wanted.

questions.prompt: Guillermo would like to go to a show that’s funny and is about a real person. He’s looking for one with some music in it, but with more speaking than singing.
questions.explanation: The Final Whistle tells the true story of a basketball player and is full of jokes and entertaining conversations. Its very few songs mean speaking is more prominent than singing.
questions.evidence: Despite being advertised as a musical show, it actually has very few songs.

questions.prompt: Neelam wants to see a musical show which contains lots of special effects and would like to watch it in an unusual place. She’d like to see a love story.
questions.explanation: No Exit uses film and advanced technology for its effects, becomes a romantic comedy and is performed in an old factory. Those features match Neelam’s wishes.
questions.evidence: the show is performed in an old factory building

questions.prompt: Oumar wants to go to a show that’s a bit frightening. He’d like to see a story set in the past and realistic costumes from the period.
questions.explanation: Mary Wright is a sixteenth-century drama with scary music and historically accurate clothes. It offers both the frightening atmosphere and realistic period setting Oumar wants.
questions.evidence: the music creates quite a scary atmosphere.

questions.prompt: Mira wants a show with dancing, as well as songs by well-known musicians. She’d like the music to be in a range of styles from around the world.
questions.explanation: Keeping Time includes the best songs of a popular group whose members came from three continents. The show combines those international musical influences with ballet.
questions.evidence: Unusually, there’s ballet in this show

parts.title: Part 3 · Long text
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Why was Louise keen to go on the trip to Canada?
questions.explanation: Louise had dreamed of visiting that area since seeing it on television as a child. She had to persuade Harry to take her and did not share his enthusiasm for boats.
questions.evidence: I’d dreamt of visiting the area ever since seeing it on TV as a child

questions.prompt: Just before their departure, Louise
questions.explanation: Although she was busy at work, Louise trusted Harry’s assurance that he had arranged everything. She therefore felt confident that they were prepared.
questions.evidence: Harry promised he’d taken care of everything, so I knew everything would be all right.

questions.prompt: On the first morning of the trip, Louise says she admired
questions.explanation: Fog prevented distant views, so Louise concentrated on the attractive patterns their boat made in the water. Her admiration was for the sea’s appearance close to them.
questions.evidence: the beautiful patterns our boat made in the water.

questions.prompt: During the trip, Louise enjoyed
questions.explanation: Louise liked being free from concern about how quickly or slowly the day passed. They still cooked meals, and the beds were hard, so those details do not support the other choices.
questions.evidence: stop caring about how quickly or slowly the day was passing.

questions.prompt: What would Louise write in her diary during the trip?
questions.explanation: The correct diary entry recalls the television programme and the family connection to the area. Both match Louise’s original reasons for wanting to visit Canada.
questions.evidence: it was where our great-grandparents had lived before moving to Europe.

parts.title: Part 4 · Missing sentences
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer. Five sentences have been removed from the text. There are three extra sentences which you do not need to use.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence for gap 16 in The Museum of Trash.
questions.explanation: G introduces the first display seen by the arriving visitors. The next sentence identifies that display as a colourful elephant made from rubbish, explaining its animated-film appearance.
questions.evidence: The first display they see looks like something out of an animated movie.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence for gap 17 in The Museum of Trash.
questions.explanation: B supplies the list of objects that visitors then try to find in the elephant. “Them all” in the following sentence refers to the objects on that list.
questions.evidence: Visitors are given a list of the different objects in it.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence for gap 18 in The Museum of Trash.
questions.explanation: The elephant represents the 900 kilograms of rubbish one person throws away in a year. H comments on how shocking it is to see that quantity represented physically.
questions.evidence: It is certainly shocking to see what that actually looks like.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence for gap 19 in The Museum of Trash.
questions.explanation: E explains where the rubbish comes from. The following phrase “these places” refers back to the twenty local towns.
questions.evidence: It comes from twenty towns in the local area.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence for gap 20 in The Museum of Trash.
questions.explanation: The director says visitors tell their friends what can be recycled. D draws the conclusion that the visit is enjoyable and also spreads useful knowledge.
questions.evidence: So while it is fun for visitors, they also pass on their new knowledge.

parts.title: Part 5 · Multiple-choice cloze
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 21 in Inventing the telephone.
questions.explanation: A system can be “developed”, meaning created or improved for a purpose. Here Bell’s father developed a system to help deaf people communicate.
questions.evidence: to help deaf people communicate.

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 22 in Inventing the telephone.
questions.explanation: The fixed pattern is “make it possible for someone to do something”. Bell wanted to enable people to talk over a distance.
questions.evidence: it possible for people to talk to each other

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 23 in Inventing the telephone.
questions.explanation: “Long distances” is the natural combination for places far apart. The other adjectives do not collocate with “distances” in this context.
questions.evidence: distances. He realised that he had to turn sound into electricity

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 24 in Inventing the telephone.
questions.explanation: Turning sound into electricity and back was a difficult engineering task, so “challenge” fits. The next paragraph also calls it a problem that required hard work.
questions.evidence: several months of hard work on this problem

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 25 in Inventing the telephone.
questions.explanation: “It” refers to the engineering problem, and we “solve” a problem. “Succeeded” would need a different construction, such as “succeeded in solving it”.
questions.evidence: after several months of hard work on this problem

questions.prompt: Choose the word for gap 26 in Inventing the telephone.
questions.explanation: “Spilt” describes accidentally letting liquid fall onto something. Bell got the dangerous liquid on his clothes while working in the laboratory.
questions.evidence: dangerous liquid on his clothes.

parts.title: Part 6 · Open cloze
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer. Write one word for each gap.

questions.prompt: Piano lessons: it’s something I’ve wanted to do ever ______ I was young.
questions.explanation: “Ever since” connects the present wish to the time in childhood when it began. It is followed here by the clause “I was young”.
questions.evidence: I was young.

questions.prompt: Piano lessons: that encouraged ______ to start lessons.
questions.explanation: “Me” is the object of “encouraged”. Harry is explaining that seeing the pianist inspired him to begin lessons himself.
questions.evidence: to start lessons.

questions.prompt: Piano lessons: I go to her house twice a week ______ lessons.
questions.explanation: “For lessons” states the purpose of going to the teacher’s house. A noun follows the preposition “for”.
questions.evidence: lessons. She’s very patient.

questions.prompt: Piano lessons: read the notes on the page and decide which piano keys to use at the ______ time!
questions.explanation: “At the same time” means doing the two activities simultaneously. Harry finds it difficult to read music while choosing the right keys.
questions.evidence: read the notes on the page and decide which piano keys to use

questions.prompt: Piano lessons: Maybe ______ day, I’ll become even better at playing the piano.
questions.explanation: Both “one day” and “some day” refer to an unspecified time in the future. Either word fits Harry’s hope about his future piano skills.
questions.evidence: day, I’ll become even better

questions.prompt: Piano lessons: I’ll become even better ______ you are at playing the piano!
questions.explanation: The comparative adjective “better” is followed by “than” when comparing two people. Harry hopes his piano playing will eventually surpass Oliver’s.
questions.evidence: you are at playing the piano!
